messages.subject: Re: Group spread CV
parts:
> > The second question I had put forward was as following:
> > I measured the perpendicular distance from line transect to the first
> > primate sighted. Following Whitesides et al. (1988) I added half of
> > the estimated group spread for the observed primate species to the
> > perpendicular distance. My question was how to incorporate the error,
> > which is induced with this method onto DISTANCE. You mentioned that
> > this is not possible directly because it is a measurement error.
> > However group spread itself is not a measurement error to he
> > perpendicular distance. For example group spread for Blue monkeys has
> > a mean of =65.7m (n=3163, CV=1.0%) If I use this mean and add half of
> > it to the perpendicular distance I induce a potential variable which I
> > need to account for in the analysis? Is it still not possible to

> > include as a multiplier?

I can't see any sensible way to add it as a multiplier, since you want an
additive effective, not a multiplicative one. (Distance groups are not
expected to have greater spreads than near ones.) Adding half the spread
to recorded perpendicular distance to the nearest animal (to the line) of
the group is OK, except for groups that span the line, for which you will
need a different procedure to identify the location of the centre of the
group. If you want to allow for uncertainty in centre location, you could
use the bootstrap: in the above case, you could resample values from say
a normal distribution with mean 65.7/2 and std error sqrt(3163)*(0.657/2).
However, this could not be done within Distance.

Steve Buckland
